Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ari Rosen (CTO - Helios), Samira Khan (ML Eng), Luis Ortega (Infra), Priya Nair (Security), Tom (PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be partial):
Helios Labs is exploring migration from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to a Dedicated Redwood deployment. Main drivers: cost predictability, data residency, lower latency for internal multi-region inference, and model/eval parity. They currently run a mix of OpenAI production + vLLM for internal batch. Concerns: compatibility with TGI/vLLM runtimes, tokenization/eval parity, SOC2/KMS integration, SSO, and migration effort. Agreed next steps include pricing/TCO, share security docs, and run a bench/egl parity test.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood, i have Maya with me, she is our solutions engineer. say hi Maya.
[00:05] Maya: hey hi all, thanks for making time.
[00:08] Ari: yeah thanks, appreciate it. we put together some notes, we'll try to keep it focused.
[00:12] Tom: quick intro from me, product manager, i own our assistant integrations.
[00:16] Jordan: great, quick agenda — understand current stack, blockers, security/compliance, and then talk about migration options: hosted -> dedicated -> private. sound good?
[00:22] Ari: yep good. so high level we use OpenAI for most prod traffic, about 1.2M requests / month, roughly 10-12B tokens. we also run an internal vLLM cluster for the heavy batch fine-tuning and some latency-sensitive inference.
[00:34] Samira: to add, some of our evaluation runs use TGI-based stacks for reproducibility. we're worried about small changes in tokenization and sampling that cause eval delta vs OpenAI.
[00:45] Maya: totally. parity is a common concern. when teams move to Dedicated we typically run your prompt set — the exact eval prompts — across our verified model variants and the OpenAI model you're comparing to, we measure generation differences, log rouge/bleu or custom metrics.
[00:58] Priya: on security — SOC2 is table stakes, we also need KMS integration, HSM optional, full audit logs, SSO via SAML + SCIM, and data residency for EU customers. we run in multi-region private clusters for some customers.
[01:12] Jordan: understood. Redwood Dedicated supports customer KMS with bring-your-own, audit logs, SAML/SCIM and RBAC. for private we can do VPC peering or full private control plane.
[01:21] Luis: what's the migration effort like — i mean we have existing code that hits OpenAI endpoints, we also have custom orchestration around vLLM locally.
[01:29] Maya: many customers keep a compatibility layer — we provide request/response parity options and SDK shims. For vLLM/TGI specifics, there are a few gotchas: sampling seeds, tokenizer differences, and certain custom kernels that change perf. we can run a side-by-side with your vLLM outputs to surface deltas.
[01:45] Samira: curious about latency, we have 95th p95 requirements of ~120ms for short chat requests. OpenAI is OK but sometimes variable; our internal vLLM gives lower tail but not SLA.
[01:56] Jordan: Dedicated can be configured for low-latency SLOs with reserved GPU pools and prioritization, plus KV cache to reduce per-token latency. we usually present expected p50/p95 numbers once we size the cluster with your traffic mix.
[02:10] Ari: cost is big — our CFO is worried about token costs vs hosting. can you provide a TCO?
[02:15] Jordan: yes, we'll run a TCO comparing continued OpenAI usage vs Redwood Dedicated committed capacity — we'll include amortized infra, support, and ops.
[02:22] Tom: about eval parity — Samira said TGI runs produce slightly different outputs. what's the typical delta you see and how to mitigate?
[02:29] Maya: a few levers: use the same model checkpoint if available, align tokenizers (we can run a diff), seed control when using sampling, and match temperature/sampling params. on the runtime side, sequence-length optimizations or kernel quantization can change logits slightly — we document those, and for some customers we lock quantization mode during parity tests.
[02:47] Samira: do you support our downstream latency-aware batching? our orchestration uses dynamic batching in vLLM.
[02:54] Maya: yes, Redwood's runtime has workload-aware batching; configs are tunable and we can expose a policy similar to yours. there might be a short ramp to tune.
[03:03] Priya: encryption at rest — do you integrate with our KMS? we cannot have plaintext keys in Redwood.
[03:09] Jordan: yes BYOK via our KMS integrations, HSM optional on Private. audit logs with object-level entries and event retention.
[03:17] Luis: any network requirements? we run inside strict VPCs with egress controls.
[03:21] Maya: Dedicated supports VPC peering, customer-managed NAT, and on-prem connectors. for strict air-gapped we have Private offerings but that is heavier.
[03:31] Ari: what's the timeline if we want to run a pilot? we want to hedge with OpenAI for 3 months but run a pilot against Redwood.
[03:38] Jordan: typical pilot is 2-6 weeks: initial sizing, pilot cluster deployment, run evals and production mirroring. we can do a canary route so some % of traffic goes to Dedicated.
[03:45] Samira: for evals can we run our prompt set across Redwood Dedicated and OpenAI to measure drift? how do you handle differences?
[03:51] Maya: yes we can run automated eval parity and provide a report with diff examples, token-level diffs, and metric regressions. we also capture raw outputs and random seeds where relevant.
[03:59] Tom: any compatibility issues with our TGI-based training artifacts?
[04:03] Maya: usually the model weights are portable; the runtime differences are more about kernels/quantization. if you use TGI's specific sampler or custom ops, we test those and sometimes run a vLLM-compatible shim for exact reproducibility.
[04:16] Ari: okay good. can you share any benchmarks for throughput/latency for models in the 7B-70B range?
[04:21] Maya: sure — i'll share our performance profiles doc after this call. note that throughput varies by sequence length, batching. we'll include expected tokens/s GPU and p50/p95 under typical loads.
[04:32] Priya: legal/procurement question — do you have standard security addendum? and what's the process for a Data Processing Agreement (DPA)?
[04:38] Jordan: yes standard security addendum and DPA templates; for enterprise we can customize. i'll include contact for legal.
[04:43] Luis: what about rollback and graceful degradation if Dedicated capacity is constrained?
[04:48] Jordan: we have smart routing — fallback to hosted or lower-cost variants automatically, and per-route policies for canary and fallback. for Dedicated customers we offer capacity bursting or cross-region failover depending on their contract.
[04:58] Samira: curious about model catalog — can we pin a specific model version? we need reproducibility for audits.
[05:04] Maya: yes we support pinned model versions and immutable model artifact references. you can do A/B rollouts and canaries with automatic rollback on regressions tied to your eval sets.
[05:14] Ari: what would you need from us to start a bench?
[05:17] Maya: your prompt set, representative traffic profile, and a few sample attachments where applicable. ideally a small prod-like dataset for latency tests.
[05:25] Samira: we'll share the prompts and a set of golden outputs.
[05:28] Jordan: perfect. i'll follow up with pricing and TCO, Maya will own compatibility notes and runbook.
[05:34] Tom: timeline — can we get the initial numbers by Friday?
[05:36] Jordan: yes we'll aim for 2026-12-11.
[05:39] Priya: thanks. one more — do you provide SIEM integrations for logs?
[05:42] Maya: yes, we can ship logs to your SIEM (splunk/elk) with configurable retention.
[05:47] Ari: ok that's helpful. anything else?
[05:50] Jordan: quick recap — action items: pricing/TCO, SOC2 + KMS docs, run eval parity bench, schedule deep dive. any objections?
[05:58] Samira: none from me.
[06:00] Priya: looks good.
[06:03] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to docs and the next meeting invite.
[06:10] [call ends]
